item.title: Dementia caregivers need stronger support, advocates say
item.dc:creator: Lourianne Graham
item.description:
Women make up two of every three primary caregivers for people with dementia worldwide, while unpaid informal care accounts for about half of the condition’s global economic cost, the Barbados…

The post Dementia caregivers need stronger support, advocates say appeared first on Barbados Today.
item.content:encoded:
Women make up two of every three primary caregivers for people with dementia worldwide, while unpaid informal care accounts for about half of the condition’s global economic cost, the Barbados Alzheimer’s Association has said.

The association drew attention to the burden on caregivers as Barbados joins the world in observing World Alzheimer’s Month.

Lawyer and advocate Kimberley Benjamin told Barbados TODAY that people living with dementia and those caring for them both have a right to care.

She said: “Care partners of persons with dementia are also generally overlooked, including in the legal rights space. Just last year, in June 2025, the Inter-American Court of Human Rights delivered a landmark ruling – Advisory Opinion AO 31/25 – that recognises the right to care as a human right.”

Kimberley Benjamin (File photo)

The court identified three dimensions of the right to care: “The right to be cared for, which means that people with care needs are entitled to quality, dignified and individualised care that respects their human rights, autonomy and privacy.

“The right to care for others, which requires that both paid and unpaid caregivers can provide care in decent conditions, free from discrimination, with access to health, work and social protection rights.

“The right to self-care, recognising that both caregivers and care recipients need the time, space and resources to look after their own physical, mental and emotional well-being.”

The court also found that care work is a protected form of work and outlined obligations for states to support both people receiving care and caregivers.

Benjamin continued: “The court emphasised that states have a duty not only to respect the right to care, but also to actively ensure its enjoyment. This includes adopting laws, policies and institutions that guarantee the rights of all people to care and be cared for, while providing enhanced protection for groups with greater care needs and for unpaid caregivers.”.

The ruling was particularly significant for people with dementia, whose care needs can increase as the condition progresses, as well as unpaid family caregivers who often have employment and household responsibilities, she added..

Benjamin said Barbados had made progress in providing home-help and day-care services through the Ministry of People Empowerment and Elder Affairs, but there was still room for improvement.

“While Barbados has made progress in providing some home help services, day care services via the Ministry of People Empowerment and Elder Affairs (Social Empowerment Agency), the policy space still has room for improvement if the environment for carers and persons with dementia is to be more inclusive.”

Alzheimer’s association executive member Kaila Branch said the financial burden of dementia care was often borne by families.
“The economic burden of dementia was US$1.3tn every year.”

About half of the global cost of dementia was linked to informal care, adding that women were disproportionately affected by the responsibility, Branch said.

“According to Alzheimer’s Disease International, two-thirds of the persons who are primary caregivers being women, and of course the women then must juggle not only the management of the person who’s living with the condition, but clearly you also have to manage the household, managing the children, managing your work, because more often than not you’re still of working age, and so therefore caregiver support is very important, and caregivers can face isolation, financial strain.”

She said caregivers needed support to protect their own wellbeing while caring for others.

“We want to put things in place because caregivers have the right to access a number of relief programmes. They have the right to ensure their own well-being as well as the well-being and dignity of the person that they’re supporting.

“And so we speak a lot, you know, not only to the right to care, but the right to be cared for.”

The Barbados Alzheimer’s Association provides support through its caregiver support group and encourages caregivers to seek help when they feel overwhelmed or need advice.

Branch said confidential support networks were important, adding that preparation and support could help families move from grief and feeling overwhelmed towards reassurance and empowerment.

The theme of World Alzheimer’s Day on Monday is The earlier you know, the more you can do: A dementia diagnosis matters. (LG)

The post Dementia caregivers need stronger support, advocates say appeared first on Barbados Today.

item.title: Dementia data gap poses challenge for care
item.dc:creator: Shamar Blunt
item.description:
Barbados needs more definitive figures on the number of people living with dementia to ensure they can receive appropriate support and care, the Barbados Alzheimer’s Association has said. Public Relations…

The post Dementia data gap poses challenge for care appeared first on Barbados Today.
item.content:encoded:
Barbados needs more definitive figures on the number of people living with dementia to ensure they can receive appropriate support and care, the Barbados Alzheimer’s Association has said.

Public Relations Officer Cyril Burke said the association is working towards improving information on dementia patients as part of its medium- to long-term goals.

Speaking to the media on the sidelines of the World Alzheimer’s Month Health and Wellness Fair on Saturday at the Main Guard Building, Garrison, Burke said having more accurate data could help the association and other agencies better respond to the needs of people with dementia, particularly during emergencies.

“We don’t have definitive figures of the amount of people in Barbados with dementia. That is challenging for us and that is something that we are trying to see if you can get around so that we can know exactly where they are for a number of different reasons,” he said.

“We’ll be able to help them better, and then in case of emergency…so if something happens, they can [get] special care. So that is what we are working on in the medium to long term to get more definitive figures on the number of people who have dementia.”

Burke said the public has been receptive to activities held during World Alzheimer’s Month, noting that many people are affected by dementia, ranging from early onset to more advanced stages.

With World Alzheimer’s Day observed on September 21, the health and wellness fair provided members of the public with access to a range of services and information.

These included blood pressure, blood sugar and cholesterol checks, body mass index assessments, cognitive screening and free PSA testing. Attendees could also receive information on dementia, its risks and prevention, as well as medical and legal advice.

Burke spoke of the importance of supporting caregivers, who he said carry significant stress while caring for someone with dementia.

He urged people to pay attention to changes in memory and behaviour, stressing that dementia involves more than the occasional experience of forgetting where an item has been placed.

He said repeated behaviour and difficulties with familiar everyday tasks could be early warning signs.

“It is when you [keep repeating] yourself. They tell you the same thing six or eight times. This is one of the early signs,” he said.

“A person could forget how to brush their teeth, how to put the belt in the pants…those kind of things. You might be making a cup of tea and you forget to put the tea bag in the cup. You forget if you’re a mom or a dad, you could forget your spouse’s name, mix up your children.”

item.title: Health Minister promotes daily movement
item.dc:creator: Shamar Blunt
item.description:
Health Minister Senator Lisa Cummins is urging Barbadians to make movement and healthier choices part of their everyday lives, saying the goal should be to keep people out of the…

The post Health Minister promotes daily movement   appeared first on Barbados Today.
item.content:encoded:
Health Minister Senator Lisa Cummins is urging Barbadians to make movement and healthier choices part of their everyday lives, saying the goal should be to keep people out of the healthcare system except when medical care is absolutely necessary.

Cummins made the call on the sidelines of Move Barbados’ “Every Body in Motion”, a free National Day of Movement held on Saturday at Queen’s Park, where families and members of the public took part in activities promoting health and wellness.

“I think you’ve heard the Ministry of Health talking and the government overall talking about building new facilities and so there’s the expansion of the Queen Elizabeth Hospital, there is a polyclinic rebuild and expansion…but if, in the Ministry of Health, we have our way, we want to keep people out of those facilities for the most part except in extreme circumstances,” she said.

Cummins said initiatives such as the movement day and Healthy Living Expo were important in encouraging Barbadians to take greater responsibility for their health.

“That’s really where healthy living comes in, and that’s where initiatives like this one that we have in partnership with the team here come in. Keeping people healthy, keeping people exposed to things they want to eat,” she said.

The Minister said one of the key messages from the event was that physical activity did not necessarily require strenuous exercise.

“One of the things about today that was really interesting, aside from the various booths that are here, it’s about helping Barbadians to understand that movement is not just big hikes or big heavy lifting, gym workouts, and that kind of thing,” Cummins said.

“It’s sometimes just moving from desk to desk internal to your office. Sometimes it’s walking up the stairs as opposed to taking the elevator.”

Cummins said the government wanted healthy habits to become part of Barbadians’ daily routines.

“We want to be able to inculcate in Barbadians on everyday for everyday purposes – move. Eat healthy, make responsible choices, and get involved,” she said.

She pointed to the range of activities and vendors at the event, including those promoting plant-based foods, as examples of how healthier living could be incorporated into everyday life.

Cummins also noted the growing number of businesses focused on health and wellness.

“When you look across the landscape of Queens Park today, you see a lot of people who are getting into [health and wellness] businesses.”

She said the response demonstrated that there was demand for healthier lifestyles but stressed that more work was needed.

“Overall the families are responding, the public, the communities are responding, but there’s always more to do because we have the highest incidence of disease burden coming from non-communicable diseases,” Cummins said.

“A lot of those things are completely avoidable by people just living healthier and making better choices.”

item.title: Captains positive ahead of CPL Final
item.dc:creator: Kurtis Hinds
item.description:
By Kurtis Hinds Both captains are confident as Antigua and Barbuda Falcons and Jamaica Kingsmen prepare to square off in Sunday’s Republic Bank Caribbean Premier League final at Kensington Oval.…

The post Captains positive ahead of CPL Final appeared first on Barbados Today.
item.content:encoded:
By Kurtis Hinds

Both captains are confident as Antigua and Barbuda Falcons and Jamaica Kingsmen prepare to square off in Sunday’s Republic Bank Caribbean Premier League final at Kensington Oval.

When the two sides met previously this season on August 7 at Sabina Park, Jamaica, the Falcons secured a thrilling two-wicket victory off the last ball of the match.

In their most recent games en route to the final, the Kingsmen defeated Guyana Amazon Warriors by five wickets in the high-scoring Qualifier 2, after the Falcons cruised to a nine-wicket win over the Amazon Warriors in Qualifier 1.

Speaking during Saturday’s pre-final media briefing, Falcons captain Moeen Ali called on his team to execute their game plan one more time this season to secure the title, with the Falcons currently unbeaten in their last five games.

“We’ve just got better and better as the tournament’s gone on. We’ve played quite consistently, but obviously, with one more game to go, anything can happen.

“Unless you win the final, coming second doesn’t really matter so much. It’s a big game against a very, very good side, and Jamaica was the most dangerous side, in my opinion,” Ali revealed.

Kingsmen captain Powell was equally complimentary of the Falcons side, which he described as full of match winners. He added that his team’s tournament plans have eventually come together nicely.

“We’re pleased to be in the final. When we sat down as a group before the start of the competition, we outlined three goals; to see if we could get into the playoffs, and then our second goal was to push to the final. The third goal was when we got to the final, to cross the line.

“When you look at it, it’s been an up-and-down run for us. I think as the competition went on, we got progressively better as the team and started finding those winning formulas,” Powell said.

The Jamaica skipper noted that Antigua played some of the best cricket during the group stage, so it was no surprise they finished as one of the top two teams before progressing to the final.

Both captains were complimentary of the playing conditions and atmosphere at Kensington Oval, with Ali adding that the CPL as a whole is very unique when compared to other T20 leagues around the world.

“It’s very different to all the other leagues in terms of the way you play and what strengths you need. In the CPL you need to play spin well; you need to have power hitters, and as bowlers, if you don’t bowl well, you can get absolutely murdered here. It’s very unique.

“There’s a lot of wind and there’s a bit of dew here and there, but those kinds of things help. There are different strengths you need, and it’s good to get some super talented players, and it’s a great place to play. The crowds are also outstanding,” Ali added.

The post Captains positive ahead of CPL Final appeared first on Barbados Today.

item.title: Sugar arrangement in limbo
item.dc:creator: Emmanuel Joseph
item.description:
Three years after signing historic agreements with the government to take over the management of the struggling sugar industry as a private operation, the cooperative involved said on Saturday it…

The post Sugar arrangement in limbo appeared first on Barbados Today.
item.content:encoded:
Three years after signing historic agreements with the government to take over the management of the struggling sugar industry as a private operation, the cooperative involved said on Saturday it may no longer be running the centuries-old sector following a recent collapse in dispute mediation talks, Barbados TODAY can report.

Chairman of the Barbados Sustainable Energy Cooperative Society (CoopEnergy) Lt Col Trevor Browne said on Saturday that the government has now abandoned the agreements signed in December 2023.

Those agreements transferred management of the state‑owned Barbados Agricultural Management Company (BAMC) to CoopEnergy and formed two private companies – Barbados Energy and Sugar Company (BESCO) Ltd. to manage the factory and Agricultural Business Company (ABC) Ltd to oversee 4 500 acres of farmland.

“This particular project, which we have been very excited about, never took off for the simple reason that we were never given any paperwork. We were never given anything that we could actually work. Obviously, based on government’s response to us, it is not going to move forward with us,” Browne told Barbados TODAY.

Asked if the cooperative will still have a role in the sugar sector, the chairman replied: “Well, if they change their mind and said that they wanted to… and that was the reason for the mediation. The mediation was a chance to say, ‘well, we don’t like how things are, but we want some things different.’ But that never came up. So, from what we are seeing, government may well be going ahead, but obviously, they don’t want to go ahead with us.”

Pressed further to state if the cooperative will have a role in the sugar industry in the future, Browne said: “[No] That is how it currently looks, based on government’s position.”

However, he insisted that the cooperative society would still want to be involved in the sugar industry if given the opportunity by the government.

Browne contends that the cooperative’s concept of managing the sector is a revolutionary one.

Asked what this development would mean for the workers and the industry he replied: “Well, I can’t speak for the workers. What it means is that government is no longer going ahead with what they had discussed at first. They might well have some other plans. You know, just like how they don’t talk to you, they don’t talk to us either. They stopped talking to us too. I can only tell you what we are doing. They are not doing anything with us. They seemed to have had a change of mind for some reason. I don’t think the workers are aware of anything. We are not.”

In a press release issued late Friday night, CoopEnergy said, “It is with a deep sense of sadness and disappointment that CoopEnergy Barbados wishes to advise the sugar workers of Barbados, and the general public at large, of the unilateral withdrawal of the Government of Barbados and the Barbados Agricultural Management Company (BAMC) from formal contractual agreements cosigned with CoopEnergy to divest the BAMC’s operations into private joint ownership by CoopEnergy and the BAMC sugar workers in the industry.”

The statement said that while this divestment was precipitated by an International Monetary Fund loan conditionality, the BAMC has been  costing  taxpayers  around  $20  million each year in subsidies to the sugar industry, and even so, was plagued with problems for many decades.

It noted that working in collaboration with BAMC leadership, CoopEnergy developed a divestment plan which was fully endorsed by the Government and cemented initially with a Memorandum of Understanding.

According to the release, extensive work was then undertaken by CoopEnergy to mobilise general support for the initiative.

Detailed presentations were held with credit unions, co‑op leaders and regulators, and advances were made with massive international resources that are available to support the cooperative movement.

Shareholders’ and Subscription Agreements creating the new companies ABC Inc. and BESCO Inc. were ﬁnally approved by Cabinet, and signed on Dec 18, 2023, coinciding with the IMF loan approval.

The cooperative said subsequent to the signing of these agreements, no formal responses to various matters raised by CoopEnergy were forthcoming from BAMC – except for a brief meeting with then Minister of Agriculture Indar Weir on September 8, 2024, following a formal letter to the minister on August 13 from the CoopEnergy Board.

“Public and private demands,” the statement continued, “were then made by BAMC and by government oﬃcials, for CoopEnergy to ‘bring money to the table’, while at the same time not providing any formal ﬁnancial records or clean asset registry for our review, as stipulated in the MOU and the Agreements.  BAMC oﬃcials also approached other cooperative bodies with invitations to provide funding and were met with the same requirement for formal ﬁnancial records to be ﬁrst provided.”

“On August 18, 2025, we received our very ﬁrst formal correspondence from BAMC advising that they had decided to ‘vitiate’ the Shareholders’ Agreements for both ABC and BESCO with immediate eﬀect.  CoopEnergy pointed out to BAMC that the signed contracts made no provision for any such unilateral ‘vitiation’, but rather required that a mediation process be used to seek to resolve any dispute that arose.  BAMC then agreed to undertake a mediation process.”

“The mediation process,” the release added, “took place between March and August 2026. It ended without any agreement between the two parties, and also without any indication that continued talks were likely to be fruitful,” CoopEnergy pointed out.

When contacted, Minister of Agriculture Dr Shantal Munro-Knight told Barbados TODAY she would have to be briefed on the matter before commenting at this stage.

In response, the Barbados Workers Union said it is not a party to the contractual agreements between the Government and BAMC, and CoopEnergy.

“We will, therefore, not comment on the details of those contracts. The BWU will continue to stand guard over the interests of the workers and to ensure that any transition, divestment or restructuring in the sugar industry honours the commitments made to them and keeps their welfare at the centre,” the BWU stated on Saturday. (EJ)

item.title: Three to appear in court on robbery, firearm charges
item.dc:creator: Barbados Today
item.description:
Three men are scheduled to appear in the District ‘A’ Criminal Court on Saturday to answer a series of joint and individual charges, including robbery, use of a firearm, serious…

The post Three to appear in court on robbery, firearm charges appeared first on Barbados Today.
item.content:encoded:
Three men are scheduled to appear in the District ‘A’ Criminal Court on Saturday to answer a series of joint and individual charges, including robbery, use of a firearm, serious bodily harm, and multiple traffic offences.

Those charged are Nathan Caleb Barker, 22, of Citrus Drive, Workmans, St George; Akeem Kareem Inniss, 23, of Bonwell Road, St Joseph; and Racaid Akeil Leroy Holder, 34, of Orange Grove, St Joseph.

Inniss, Holder, and Barker have been jointly charged with using a firearm, robbery, and inflicting serious bodily harm in a September 12 incident in District ‘B’.

Inniss and Holder are also jointly accused of using a firearm and committing robbery the previous day.

Inniss faces additional charges stemming from a separate incident in Belleplaine, District ‘F’, on September 12, including driving without insurance, driving without a licence, driving without reasonable consideration, driving without due care and attention, and failing to comply with a beacon and siren.

item.title: BKA karters back on Bushy Park track this Sunday
item.dc:creator: Barbados Today
item.description:
The Barbados Karting Association’s Sectus Technologies Championship returns to action on Sunday, September 20, with round five of the eight-round series at Bushy Park. The event marks the end of…

The post BKA karters back on Bushy Park track this Sunday appeared first on Barbados Today.
item.content:encoded:
The Barbados Karting Association’s Sectus Technologies Championship returns to action on Sunday, September 20, with round five of the eight-round series at Bushy Park.

The event marks the end of a three-month break for local competitors, who return to domestic competition following last month’s Nations Cup Caribbean in Trinidad and Tobago.

Barbados finished second to the hosts at the Nations Cup, with 14-year-old Aeden Bruce emerging as the only driver to complete all six races. He recorded three podium finishes and three additional top-five results.

He was the most successful of the visiting drivers and second in the individual competition to Trinidad and Tobago’s Jonathan Sharam.

Bruce, the 2025 BKA 100cc champion, returns to local action looking to improve on his third-place standing in the Easykart 125cc category.

It is his first season in the class, where he faces more experienced competitors Aaron Blackett and former champion Jacob Mayers, who occupy first and second place respectively in the standings. Mayers, however, will miss the remainder of the season as he pursues his education overseas.

Also keen to better their current positions are Bruce’s fellow Nations Cup team members Jordyn Hinkson and Jaylan Priddee, who are second and third in the Easykart 100cc standings behind Jaydn Brathwaite.

Overall leader of the Champion Driver title chase, Edward Norris, leads the ever-competitive Easykart 60cc Cadets class, which has three drivers in the top six overall.

Second in the class and fourth overall is Ava Mayers, who in April became the first female karter in the BKA’s 40-year history to finish as the top points scorer in a round. Finn Cox is third in the class and fifth overall. (PR/KH)

item.title: Five juveniles remanded, another on bail
item.dc:creator: Barbados Today
item.description:
Five of six juveniles accused of committing 24 offences — ranging from the use of a firearm to the theft of a motor vehicle—across four policing districts have been remanded…

The post Five juveniles remanded, another on bail appeared first on Barbados Today.
item.content:encoded:
Five of six juveniles accused of committing 24 offences — ranging from the use of a firearm to the theft of a motor vehicle—across four policing districts have been remanded to the Barbados Prison Service at Dodds, while the sixth was granted $2 000 bail.

Four of the juveniles appeared before Magistrate (ag) Jared Richards in the District ‘A’ Traffic Court on Thursday, with the remaining two appearing before Chief Magistrate Douglas Frederick the previous day. All six are scheduled to return to court on October 15, 2026.

The charges stem from incidents recorded between April and September this year.

In the Hastings/Worthing district, the juveniles are alleged to have endangered life on June 3, June 8, three times on July 4, and again on July 20.

They are also accused of wounding with intent on July 5, aggravated burglary on June 3, and several robberies committed on February 7, July 20, August 5, August 18, and August 31.

Police have further charged them with using a firearm during incidents on June 3, June 8, July 4, and July 5, as well as the theft of a motor vehicle on August 31.

In the Central district, the allegations include a robbery on August 22, assault with intent to rob on September 6, two counts of assaulting a police officer on September 7, and resisting a police officer on the same date.

Charges laid in Black Rock relate to wounding with intent and the use of a firearm during an incident on April 7, along with escaping lawful custody.

A separate motor vehicle theft charge was brought in relation to an incident in District ‘A’ on August 31.

item.title: Citizens invited to nominate national honours recipients
item.dc:creator: Shamar Blunt
item.description:
A new national honour is being minted to mark the country’s 60th anniversary of Independence and five years as a Republic, honouring Barbadians who have made exceptional contributions to nation-building,…

The post Citizens invited to nominate national honours recipients appeared first on Barbados Today.
item.content:encoded:
A new national honour is being minted to mark the country’s 60th anniversary of Independence and five years as a Republic, honouring Barbadians who have made exceptional contributions to nation-building, the Cabinet Office announced on Friday. 

Dubbed the Barbados Diamond Anniversary Honour, it will recognise citizens whose distinguished or sustained service, leadership or exceptional achievements have made a significant contribution to national development.

Cabinet Secretary Selma Green made the announcement during the media launch of the National Calendar of Independence Celebrations at Ilaro Court, where she also revealed that nominations are open for the 2026 National Independence Honours.

The special Diamond Anniversary Honour would recognise contributions across areas including public service, education, health, business, culture, sport, community development, science and technology, national security, charitable service and the Barbadian diaspora, she said.

Eligible nominees must be Barbadian citizens who have demonstrated distinguished or sustained service, integrity, leadership, exemplary conduct or exceptional achievement.

But, Green noted that people who already hold a national honour or decoration are not eligible for the Barbados Diamond Anniversary Honour.

She encouraged Barbadians to look beyond the country’s most familiar names when considering nominees.

She said: “As we commemorate 60 years of Independence and five years as a Republic, we’re reminded that the story of Barbados is ultimately the story of its people – those who have served, sacrificed, led, created, cared and worked often quietly and without expectation of recognition to build this beautiful nation.”

She described national honours and decorations as “one of the most meaningful ways in which we as a grateful nation can say thank you”.

The National Independence Honours would recognise outstanding achievement and meritorious service across all areas of national life, Green said. 

“I particularly encourage Barbadians to look beyond the familiar names,” she said, urging people to consider those making a difference in their communities, professions, churches, schools, sporting organisations and voluntary groups.

She pointed to teachers who have shaped generations, community workers who have served quietly for decades, artistes who have preserved the country’s culture, entrepreneurs who have created opportunities, and public and protective services officers who have exemplified duty.

Green also encouraged nominations of Barbadians whose contributions have brought distinction to the country.

Nominations for both the National Independence Honours and the Barbados Diamond Anniversary Honour close next Friday.

Applications can be submitted electronically through the government’s online nomination form, which will be promoted through the Barbados Government Information Service and other government digital platforms.

Citizens requiring assistance can also contact the Cabinet Office.

(SB)

The post Citizens invited to nominate national honours recipients appeared first on Barbados Today.

item.title: Blackman and Gollop pupils in national tree-planting drive
item.dc:creator: Shamar Blunt
item.description:
Blackman and Gollop Primary School pupils joined Barbados Defence Force soldiers and sailors to plant 65 shade trees on Friday, as Barbados advances a monthly national effort ahead of its…

The post Blackman and Gollop pupils in national tree-planting drive appeared first on Barbados Today.
item.content:encoded:
Blackman and Gollop Primary School pupils joined Barbados Defence Force soldiers and sailors to plant 65 shade trees on Friday, as Barbados advances a monthly national effort ahead of its “60 and Five” celebrations on November 30.

The initiative forms part of a partnership between the BDF and the National Conservation Commission (NCC) to plant 65 trees every month leading up to November 30, when Barbados will celebrate the 60th anniversary of Independence and five years as a Republic.

Principal Harriet Blackman said 36 students from Classes 1 to 4 took part in the exercise, with each student paired with a BDF officer.

“I am pleased to be part of the Tree Planet exercise for 60 and five. We have 36 students here participating in the tree-planting exercise, and I’m happy that the school has been selected to be part of this,” she told Barbados TODAY.

The exercise gave the students an opportunity to participate in a national initiative while also supporting the school’s environmental goals, she said.

“It serves to help them to be part of something national.

“We are gonna strive to do our best to keep these trees because it fits in with our mandate that we have in terms of tree planting, also providing shade for the school, and it will also encourage our students to look after our environment.”

She said giving the students responsibility for the trees would help them develop a stronger connection to the environment.

“They will have a stake in it and therefore it will help them to remember the importance of it.”

The project is also expected to create a new outdoor learning space on the school’s compound.

“As we prepare the space this morning, it also serves for us down the line as an outdoor classroom with shade,” Blackman said.

“We’re hoping that as we go down the line we can place some benches, some tables, and encourage our teachers and our students to use the space for educational purposes and also for recreation.”

Dewyn Phillips, coordinator of the National Tree Planting Programme in the Ministry of Environment, said the ministry was pleased to be working with the BDF on the initiative.

He said the partnership brought together three important areas — national security, education and environmental conservation.

“It’s a collaborative effort, basically one of the Defence Force, where we look at protection of the boundaries, one of the schools which represents education, and the one of NCC which would represent environmental conservation. 

“These three…we are looking at these synergies, [and] looking to push forward for every month leading up to Independence Day.”

Phillips said there were hopes of taking the tree-planting initiative to additional schools before the November 30 celebrations.

(SB)

The post Blackman and Gollop pupils in national tree-planting drive appeared first on Barbados Today.
